query: films criticised for underexposed cinematography audience reaction

results.title: IndieWire - The DP explains why that battle was shot so dark
results.text: The director of photography defended the lighting choices, saying the crew knew it would be dark in order to capture the claustrophobic fog of war. Viewers on consumer televisions saw crushed blacks instead, because low-bitrate streaming turns fine shadow detail into grey blocks.

results.title: The Ringer - Fight Club at 25: the underexposure was the point
results.text: Critics who revisited the film agree the murky, green-tinged underexposure is deliberate authorship rather than a defect, and audiences have never held the darkness against it. The look reads as intentional grime, and that intention is why the film is still cited as a landmark of studio cinematography.

results.title: r/movies - Are unreliable-narrator twists played out now?
results.text: Top comment with 3,100 upvotes: the unreliable narrator reveal is the single most predicted twist of the last decade, and audiences now spend the second act hunting for it instead of following the story.
